prompt: A circle has radius $8$ and center $O$. From a point $P$ that is $17$ units from $O$, a tangent line touches the circle at point $T$. How long is $\overline{PT}$?
hint: A radius drawn to the point of tangency is perpendicular to the tangent line — there is a right angle at $T$.

hints.text: A radius drawn to the point of tangency is perpendicular to the tangent line — there is a right angle at $T$.
So $\triangle OTP$ is right-angled at $T$, with hypotenuse $OP = 17$ and leg $OT = 8$.

explanation: The tangent meets the radius $\overline{OT}$ at a right angle, so $\triangle OTP$ is a right triangle.
The hypotenuse is $OP = 17$ (it faces the right angle) and one leg is the radius $8$.

alternativeExplanations.title: Which side is the hypotenuse?
steps: The right angle is at $T$, so the side across from it — $\overline{OP}$, the $17$ — is the hypotenuse.
Because the hypotenuse is known, you subtract: $17^2 - 8^2$, landing on the $8$-$15$-$17$ triple.
